idea: AI equity-analysis tool for SMID caps
buyer: Analysts and PMs, sold per seat
pain: SMID names are poorly covered by existing research platforms
v1: A web tool that ingests filings and drafts an initiation
channel: The Substack list from stage 1 - which does not exist yet
verdict: Marginal. A genuinely hard software business for a non-engineer, competing against well-funded incumbents on distribution she has not yet built.

why.distribution: Depends on a subscriber list stage 1 has not produced. Score what exists: newsletter readers are not automatically tool buyers, so this is adjacency again.
why.demand: Analysts do pay for tools and budgets exist, but the segment is crowded and nothing has been tested.
why.fmf: She knows the workflow and has led AI adoption for exactly this user, but she is not a production software engineer shipping and supporting an external product.
why.revenue_structure: Per-seat SaaS subscription with ordinary churn.
why.defensibility: A layer over a foundation model in a category where Rogo, Hebbia, AlphaSense and Fiscal.ai are funded and shipping, and where the model providers ship the same feature natively. What does she own when they do?
why.leverage: Genuine software economics - one build serves every seat.
why.capital: Real engineering before anyone pays: £10-30k contracted, more if it needs support.
why.time_to_revenue: Build then sell: 9-12 months before meaningful revenue.
why.tailwind: AI adoption spend in professional services is real and has budget attached.
why.ceiling: £100/seat/month x 200 seats = £240k gross, but 200 paying seats in year one with no existing list is optimistic; £100-200k is the honest range.

ceiling_arithmetic: £100/seat/month = £1.2k/yr. 200 seats = £240k gross. Reaching 200 paying seats in year one from no list, against funded incumbents, is optimistic - £100-200k is the honest band, and that assumes the build lands on time.
carries: True software leverage and a real AI-adoption tailwind with budget attached.
kills: Defensibility at 1. It is a thin layer over a foundation model in the most crowded corner of AI-for-finance, and it would eat the product of stage 1 - if AI can do SMID analysis well enough to sell as a tool, it can write the deep dives too.
test: Before building anything, ask ten of the same PMs whether they would pay per seat for a SMID-specific tool, and what they already use. The answer is usually 'we have AlphaSense' - which is the finding.
test_pass: Several name a specific gap their current stack does not fill and put a number on it.
test_fail: They describe workflows already covered by an incumbent, or say they would rather buy the research than the tool.
reshape: Sell the tool's output as a service (the institutional research variant) rather than the tool itself - same insight, no engineering risk, revenue in month two instead of month eleven.
flags: Competing directly with well-funded incumbents and with the model providers themselves.
